key_insight: The paper shows that connecting flat planar quantum modules with sparse boundary links can deliver high-rate, low-overhead quantum error correction without relying on fully non-local hardware.
engineering_relevance: This modular design could dramatically reduce the number of physical qubits needed for fault-tolerant quantum memory while preserving the manufacturability advantages of mostly nearest-neighbor planar layouts.
method: Build semi-hyperbolic surface and color codes from Euclidean planar modules joined by static boundary connections
Use modular syndrome extraction circuits with neural-network and matching decoders
Co-design fault-tolerant walking circuits and low-weight logical bases for efficient logical operations
evidence_signal: Circuit-level simulations indicate about a tenfold or greater qubit-overhead reduction versus the surface code, and projected larger instances achieve rate k/n = 1/16 with distance d ≥ 22 and over 30× overhead reduction.
watch_item: The approach depends on seam/inter-module connection quality and added circuit complexity, so performance may be sensitive to elevated boundary error rates and hardware integration constraints.
paper_title: Low-Overhead Quantum Error Correction with Boundary-Connected Planar Modules
